name: Wrong Way, Right Way Split
why_it_works: People check themselves against the wrong side first: 'wait, that's how I do it.' That flash of self-recognition is the hook. Seeing the right way next to it makes the difference obvious without a lecture, and viewers comment to confess which side they were on.

hook.pattern: Split the screen, mark one side with an X and one with a check, and ask which one the viewer does.
examples: Left or right: how do you {{task}}?
You're probably doing the left one.
Two ways to {{task}}. One ruins it.

variables.name: task
variables.description: The everyday task, as a lowercase verb phrase, 4 words or fewer

variables.name: wrong_way
variables.description: The common wrong way, starting with a capital letter, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: In a clear jar by the window

variables.name: right_way
variables.description: The right way, starting with a capital letter, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: In an opaque airtight bag, away from light and heat

variables.name: why_difference
variables.description: Why the right way wins, one sentence, 15 words or fewer
variables.example: Light and air stale beans within days, flattening the flavor you paid for

variables.name: self_check
variables.description: A yes/no question viewers can ask themselves to spot the wrong way, 12 words or fewer
variables.example: Can you see your beans right now? Then light can too.

variables.name: pro_tip
variables.description: One save-worthy tip the reel does not cover, 15 words or fewer
variables.example: Buy only what you will brew in two weeks, and check the roast date.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: Next step or product tie-in, starting with a verb, 6 words or fewer
variables.example: Ask for this week's roast date

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

beats.purpose: hook: split screen, X and check
beats.voiceover: Be honest. Which way do you {{task}}?

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 split-screen photo: left side shows '{{wrong_way}}' with a red X, right side shows '{{right_way}}' with a green check, matching angle and framing on both sides, clean neutral background

beats.purpose: the wrong way and its cost

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 slow push-in on someone doing '{{wrong_way}}', cool flat light, slightly desaturated, eye-level mid shot
Vertical 9:16 smooth close-up of hands doing '{{right_way}}', warm natural light, rich color, shallow depth of field, confident unhurried motion
Vertical side-by-side result photo: the outcome of the wrong way next to the outcome of the right way, top-down, same light, clear visible difference

cta: Tell us which side you were on, then switch. {{offer}}.

slides.headline: Left or right?
slides.visual_prompt: Split-screen photo with '{{wrong_way}}' on the left marked with a red X and '{{right_way}}' on the right marked with a green check

slides.headline: The wrong way
slides.visual_prompt: Photo of '{{wrong_way}}' in cool flat light, slightly desaturated, red X in the corner

slides.headline: Why it fails
slides.visual_prompt: Close-up showing the damage or poor result from the wrong way, natural light, detail visible

slides.headline: The right way
slides.visual_prompt: Photo of hands doing '{{right_way}}' in warm natural light, green check in the corner

slides.headline: Quick self-check
slides.visual_prompt: Simple question card in {{brand}} colors with a large question mark and a yes/no tick box

slides.headline: Save this tip
slides.visual_prompt: Clean tip card in {{brand}} colors with a bookmark icon and one bold line of text

slides.headline: Switch sides today
slides.visual_prompt: Clean {{brand}} logo card with the offer in large type

craft.notes: Shoot both sides at the identical angle, distance and framing, changing only the light and the action. When everything else matches, the eye goes straight to the one difference. Cool, flat light on wrong; warm light on right. The carousel adds a self-check and a tip the reel skips.

do_not: Make the wrong way look absurd; it has to be what normal people actually do
Show a wrong way that risks injury (bad lifting form, hot tools on skin) without a clear safety caption
Pick a 'right way' that is only a matter of taste
compliance: Skincare: cosmetic claims only; never say a routine treats acne, eczema or any condition unless the product is approved for it
Fitness: add 'Consult a professional before starting a new exercise' when showing form corrections; no guaranteed body results
